questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Double Column Cash Book with Bank Column' refers to.
questions.a: A double column cash book carries cash and bank columns on both sides, records cheques received and deposited, and shows a credit bank balance as bank overdraft when payments exceed deposits.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Double Column Cash Book with Bank Column'.
questions.a: Contra entries, marked with C, record cash deposited into or withdrawn from the bank and affect both columns without touching the final result.

concepts.title: Petty Cash Book and the Imprest System

questions.q: Using the method 'Petty Cash Book and the Imprest System', work with: imprest_amount = 500, petty_cash_in_hand = 6. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of petty_reimbursement.

Take the relation taught for 'Petty Cash Book and the Imprest System' and work with: imprest_amount = 50000, petty_cash_in_hand = 10. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of petty_reimbursement.
Explain in your own words what 'Petty Cash Book and the Imprest System' refers to.
questions.a: The petty cash book records small repetitive payments under analytical columns such as postage, conveyance and stationery; under the imprest system the petty cashier is reimbursed exactly the amount spent, restoring the float to its fixed amount.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Petty Cash Book and the Imprest System'.
questions.a: The chief cashier advances the imprest amount, and the petty cashier reports expenses column-wise, which reduces the main cash book's size.
